title: When Harnesses Lose the Signal: Causal Evaluation of Recovery in LLM Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.00372v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language model agents rely on external harnesses to pass information between the model and its environment and to recover from execution errors. Yet recovery is usually judged only by average task success. This hides an important tension. The same operation can rescue a failing trajectory or disrupt one that would otherwise succeed. We frame recovery as a causal decision problem. Starting from the same execution state, we compare what happens with and without recovery, separate rescue from harm, and study how the value of recovery changes over time. We then introduce the Causal Intervention Router (CIR), a lightweight policy that uses information available before recovery to decide when intervention is worthwhile. On long-horizon ALFWorld tasks with Qwen3-14B, CIR raises success from 70.33% to 73.33%, a gain of 3.00 percentage points. It leaves all evaluated trajectories with correct observations untouched. translated_title: 当执行框架失去信号时：LLM智能体恢复的因果评估
translated_abstract: 摘要：大型语言模型（LLM）智能体依赖外部执行框架在模型与环境之间传递信息，并从执行错误中恢复。然而，恢复效果通常仅以平均任务成功率来评判，这掩盖了一个重要的矛盾：同一操作既可能挽救一条即将失败的执行轨迹，也可能破坏一条本会成功的轨迹。我们将恢复问题构建为一个因果决策问题：从同一执行状态出发，比较进行恢复与不进行恢复时的结果，区分“挽救”与“损害”，并研究恢复价值随时间的变化。随后，我们提出了因果干预路由器，这是一种轻量级策略，利用恢复之前可获得的信息来判断何时进行干预才是值得的。在使用Qwen3-14B模型的长程ALFWorld任务上，CIR将成功率从70.33%提升至73.33%，提高3.00个百分点，并且对所有观察结果正确的评估轨迹保持不干预。额外的对照实验显示
tldr: 该论文将LLM智能体的错误恢复重新框定为因果决策问题，并提出轻量级的因果干预路由器（CIR），利用恢复前的信息判断干预时机——只挽救失败轨迹而不干扰本会成功的轨迹，使长程ALFWorld任务成功率提升3个百分点。
en_tdlr: This paper reframes LLM agent error recovery as a causal decision problem and introduces the lightweight Causal Intervention Router (CIR), which uses pre-recovery information to intervene only when beneficial—rescuing failing trajectories without disrupting successful ones—improving long-horizon ALFWorld success by 3 percentage points.
